market_summary: S&P 500 -2.02%, Nasdaq -2.25%, Dow -2.19% (-1,101 pts, below 50,000), sixth straight S&P loss; early Anthropic-IPO gains reversed into an AI selloff and all 11 sectors fell. 10yr eased to 5.05%. Fed December odds not confirmed from a Nov 19 source; reports cite reduced easing expectations. US stocks sold off hard on Nov 19: S&P 500 -2.0% to 7,176, Nasdaq -2.25%, Dow -2.2%, as Nvidia (-3.3%) stayed under pressure after Jensen Huang's Nov 12 resignation and new SEC and California probes, despite record Q3 revenue of $115.8B and a ~$130B Q4 guide. Semis led the losses (AMD -7.7%, AVGO -2.1%), Anthropic's Nasdaq debut (+17%) gave AI only a brief lift, and a new US rule blocks Chinese firms from renting advanced AI chips through overseas data centres. Rates are a headwind: FOMC minutes showed nearly all officials expect more hikes and a December hike is priced, so Oct PCE on Nov 25 is the key print. Trump and Xi met in Shenzhen but did not extend the trade truce (expires Jan 10, 2027) and left chips and rare earths out; the Trump-Xi-Putin statement pushed more oil supply, which weighs on energy prices. AI capex demand still looks intact on Nvidia's numbers, but the market is pricing governance and regulatory risk over growth.

headlines: S&P 500 fell 2.0% Nov 19, sixth straight loss; Nasdaq -2.25%, Dow -1,101 points as the AI trade reversed.
Anthropic closed +17% on its Nasdaq debut after opening 34% above the $83 IPO price.
Every holding fell: NVDA -3.3% despite record Q3, MRVL -4.9% on two downgrades, LDI -7.4%.
Trump-Xi APEC meeting did not extend the trade truce; it still expires Jan 10.
